setup: Set the pins or blocks so the bar sits near your knees
Mid-foot under the bar, feet hip-width
Hinge and grip just outside your legs
Chest up, back flat, arms straight
execution: Breathe in and brace before each pull
Push the floor away and drive your hips forward
Keep the bar close to your thighs
Lower under control back to the pins
faults: Don't round your back to reach the bar
Don't lean back hard at the top
Don't slam or bounce the bar on the pins

notes: Set both pins at the same height and check they're locked before loading. Blocks or stacked plates are gentler on the bar and rack than steel pins.
Rack pulls usually allow more weight than a deadlift. Add load gradually, and end the set when your back can't stay flat.
Straps are fine when grip gives out before your back and legs.
Bar height changes the lift. Note it (for example below or above the knee) so sessions compare like with like.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Bar on the pins at about knee height, over mid-foot. Hips hinged back, knees slightly bent, shins near vertical. Back flat, chest up, arms straight.

keyPositions.label: Lockout
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, hips and knees straight, shoulders over the hips. Bar at the upper thighs, arms straight. No backward lean.

ikHints: Bar stays in contact with or close to the thighs
guideBrief.barPath: Vertical over mid-foot, from the pins to the upper thigh
emphasise: Flat back from start to finish
Hips drive forward to stand tall
